incidents.summary:
The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has now surpassed 7,000 confirmed cases and nearly 3,400 deaths, with a case detected in a seventh province, South-Ubangi, bordering the Central African Republic and Congo-Brazzaville. Despite the U.S. allocating hundreds of millions of dollars and vaccine trials underway, deaths continue to climb, though government officials suggest transmission may have peaked. The outbreak remains the second largest in history and the second deadliest, with the updated case count reaching 7,200.
New reports as of mid-September 2026 indicate the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has surpassed 7,200 confirmed cases, though some sources note an overall downward trend despite worsening conditions in North Kivu. The UN warns the outbreak remains "massive" and will take months to contain, while aid officials acknowledge partial success in limiting spread in other areas.

logs.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the fastest-growing ever, with cases surging above 1,000 and the death toll reaching 600. The outbreak has spread to new provinces including Tshopo and Haut-Uele, and the first case outside Africa has been confirmed in France. Response efforts are hampered by funding shortages, unpaid health workers, and the closure of USAID, while new diagnostic tests and treatment trials offer hope.

news.headline: Médecins Sans Frontières Launches 'Keep Life Breathing' Roving Exhibition to Spotlight Humanitarian Crises and Ebola Disease Outbreak in DRC
news.body: HONG KONG, July 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) Hong Kong yesterday held an opening ceremony for its 'Keep Life Breathing' Roving Exhibition. As a key part of its annual 'MSF Day' campaign, the exhibition will tour three locations throughout July: The Wai, Festival Walk, and TKO Plaza. It showcases real-life stories of MSF providing emergency medical humanitarian assistance to people affected by protracted conflicts and crises. The event also features an Ebola disease-themed zone, which aims to deepen public awareness and understanding of the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has now surpassed 7,000 confirmed cases and nearly 3,400 deaths, with a case detected in a seventh province, South-Ubangi, bordering the Central African Republic and Congo-Brazzaville. Despite the U.S. allocating hundreds of millions of dollars and vaccine trials underway, deaths continue to climb, though government officials suggest transmission may have peaked. The outbreak remains the second largest in history and the second deadliest, with the updated case count reaching 7,200.
New reports as of mid-September 2026 indicate the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has surpassed 7,200 confirmed cases, though some sources note an overall downward trend despite worsening conditions in North Kivu. The UN warns the outbreak remains "massive" and will take months to contain, while aid officials acknowledge partial success in limiting spread in other areas.

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

logs.summary:
A severe drought is affecting multiple regions globally as of late July 2026. In Europe, an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit half of England and all of Wales, while the Rhine River dropped to its lowest ever level in the Netherlands and the Danube reached record lows in Budapest, disrupting tourism and industry. In the United States, drought conditions worsened in states like Minnesota and Michigan, while other areas like the Grand Strand in South Carolina are lifting drought management plans, and parts of Virginia and North Carolina are seeing improvements.
New drought developments include worsening conditions in Maine and Minnesota, with 35% of Minnesota in severe drought, while South Carolina's Lowcountry remains under extreme drought despite summer storms. In Europe, record-low river levels continue to disrupt power output and transport, and wildfire risk is elevated across the continent. Jamaica faces a potential $500 million drought response, and drone footage highlights the drought's impact in England.

news.headline: Record-low Danube River affects tourism and industry as drought and heat grip Central Europe
news.body: As wildfires and successive heatwaves in France and Spain highlight climate change's impact, a severe drought is causing record low water levels on the Danube River, affecting tourism and industry. The river, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows, exposing rocks and old shipwrecks. In Budapest, the Danube was measured at just 23 centimeters, breaking previous records. River cruise ships are docking upriver, and sightseeing cruises have been canceled. The drought has also affected Hungary and Romania's nuclear power plant operations, exposed a World War II bomb, and ended the summer season for excursion boat operators in Serbia.

logs.summary:
Greece faced severe wildfires in late July and early August 2026, with a major blaze northwest of Athens destroying over 100 homes and burning thousands of hectares. On August 2, two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air near Psatha, killing two crew members. By August 3, water-dropping aircraft continued to battle the fires, which had been fueled by extreme winds and record-breaking heat, with over 200 fires reported across the country since July 27.
On August 3, the wildfire west of Athens flared up again, requiring continued water-bombing aircraft operations. By August 4, firefighters seized a break in high winds to reinforce containment lines, while some residents returned to damaged homes, though forecasters warned that stronger gusts and rising temperatures were expected to return. The blaze, part of over 200 fires across Greece since late July, remained a threat amid a record-breaking heatwave and drought.

news.headline: Wildfires Rage in Greece as Heat Wave Grips Europe
news.body: In Greece, two firefighters were killed Sunday when two helicopters battling a massive wildfire collided west of Athens. Two other crew members in one of the helicopters were rescued. More than 100 homes were destroyed overnight this weekend in blazes that broke out around the coastal village of Porto Germeno. Hundreds of people have been evacuated. This is a local resident. Giorgos Mavroidis: “It’s not a good situation. This is extremely sad. The wind is very strong and keeps changing direction. It’s difficult to deal with. The firefighters, who are trained and experienced, can’t contain it. How can we?” Meanwhile, Hungary has temporarily shut down the country’s sole nuclear power plant for the first time in more than four decades amid a scorching heat wave and severe drought that triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages. In more related news, Britain’s National Farmers’ Union warns rising heat and a water drought could lead to shortages of certain foods in parts of England. This is at least the third drought in five years, with some areas of England not seeing rain in over a month. Here in the United States, in Washington state, nearly 65,000 people have received evacuation orders amid intensifying wildfires around the city of Spokane. Local officials say blazes in the region have destroyed more than 700 homes and businesses.

incidents.summary: Canada's 2026 wildfire burn area exceeded the 10-year average, reaching 4.48 million hectares. New fires emerged in northwestern Ontario, with the Rinker Complex remaining uncontained, and a new forest fire in Port Hope Simpson, Newfoundland, prompted evacuation preparations. Fire activity picked up on the Ainslie Creek blaze near Merritt, British Columbia, while Ontario wildfire smoke drove Michigan's AQI to 616, and Prime Minister Carney acknowledged the need for stronger responses to severe wildfire seasons.

logs.summary: In early August 2026, wildfires in western Canada, particularly the Bald Range fire near Summerland, British Columbia, escalated dramatically. The fire burned over 33,000 acres, destroyed approximately 230 homes, and resulted in the death of one woman, prompting evacuation orders for around 20,000 people. In response, British Columbia declared a state of emergency as crews faced challenging conditions from severe drought and windy weather.

news.body: BOGOTÁ, Colombia (AP) — Colombia's President Abelardo de la Espriella has asked U.S. President Donald Trump to suspend tariffs to help Colombia recover from a devastating earthquake. The 7.4 magnitude quake struck Monday, killing at least 289 people and injuring nearly 4,000. De la Espriella, who took office earlier this month, emphasized his connections with Trump, thanking him for $26.5 million in U.S. aid. The quake destroyed thousands of homes, including in western cities like Pereira and Cali. The government declared it a natural disaster, with at least143 people missing and extensive damage reported. Rescue efforts continue despite the challenging conditions.

logs.summary: Severe thunderstorms, tornadoes, and flash flooding impacted multiple regions across the United States from August 20–24, 2026. Confirmed tornadoes struck in Atlantic Beach (Long Island), Dover (Delaware), and York/Lancaster counties (Pennsylvania), while prolonged power outages from earlier storms left thousands without electricity in Gary, Indiana, for over a week. Widespread damage from downed trees, damaged homes, and flooding was reported in the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Southeast, and Midwest.

news.headline: Severe thunderstorm watch issued for west-central Saskatchewan
news.body: Environment Canada has issued a severe thunderstorm watch for west-central Saskatchewan as conditions become favourable for storms capable of producing strong wind gusts, large hail and heavy rain. The watch was issued at 3:03 p.m. Friday and carries a moderate impact level with high forecast confidence. Environment Canada says a trough of low pressure moving across southwestern Saskatchewan is expected to trigger thunderstorms late Friday afternoon and into the evening. Some of those storms could become severe. A severe thunderstorm watch means conditions are favourable for storms capable of producing damaging hail, strong winds or heavy rainfall, but does not mean severe weather is occurring everywhere in the watch area. Environment Canada is asking residents to continue monitoring forecasts and alerts as conditions develop. Severe weather reports can be submitted to Environment Canada through #SKStorm on social media, by email at SKstorm@ec.gc.ca or by calling 1-800-239-0484.

logs.summary:
A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia's Flores region near Ende on August 14, 2026, toppling buildings and killing at least two people. The shallow quake triggered a tsunami warning for four provinces, prompting mass evacuations before the alert was later lifted. Several strong aftershocks were reported.
The death toll from the magnitude 7.7 earthquake near Ende, Indonesia has risen to at least 38, with dozens injured and many buildings collapsed or damaged. Rescuers are searching for survivors in affected areas, and tsunami waves of less than 1 meter were recorded in several locations before the warning was lifted.

news.headline: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off Indonesia, tsunami warning issued - West Hawaii Today
news.body: JAKARTA (Reuters) — An earthquake of magnitude 7.7 and several aftershocks struck off the coast of eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, the nation’s geophysics agency BMKG said, while tsunami waves of less than 1 metre (3 feet) were recorded in several areas. Many rushed from their homes, but there were no initial reports of damage from the quake, which was felt strongly for around one minute in regions such as Nagekeo and Bima, said Dodi Yuleova, the spokesperson for the national disaster mitigation agency. A video on Facebook, verified by Reuters as located at a port in Maumere, the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in eastern Indonesia, showed parts of a building collapsing in dust and rubble as people screamed and ran in the street. A hospital in the district of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara Province was moving patients outside, Kompas TV footage showed. BMKG recorded the first quake at 4:58 a.m. (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15 km (9 miles), followed by several aftershocks.

logs.summary: Severe monsoon rains and cyclones have caused widespread flooding across the Philippines, particularly in Luzon, with damage nearing P4 billion in Central Luzon and P2.68 billion in infrastructure damage in the Ilocos Region, affecting over four million people. At least two brothers drowned in a submerged bypass road in Pampanga, and a baby was dramatically rescued from flash floods in Manila. In response, lawmakers are pushing for flood control master plan reviews and Senate investigations into the government's disaster response.

news.body: Indonesia’s Anak Krakatau volcano erupted early Sunday, prompting the cancellation of all flights at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and disrupting other domestic airports as volcanic ash drifted across parts of western Indonesia. Indonesia’s Geological Agency said the volcanic island located in Indonesia’s Sunda Strait between the main Java and Sumatra islands had showed signs of activity since Friday before erupting for 30 seconds at 3:53 a.m. Sunday. Closed-circuit camera footage showed lava flares from the volcano.

news.headline: MAMAMOO’s Concert In Jakarta Cancelled
news.body: MAMAMOO’s upcoming concert in Jakarta has been canceled. The group’s “4WARD” concert in Jakarta, which was scheduled to take place at NICE PIK 2 on September 19, 2026, has been canceled due to ongoing unpredictable circumstances following recent volcanic activity in Indonesia. Read RBW’s full statement below: Hello, this is RBW. We regret to inform you that the “MAMAMOO 2026 WORLD TOUR <4WARD> in JAKARTA,” which was scheduled to take place at NICE PIK 2 on September 19, 2026, has been canceled due to unavoidable circumstances. Due to recent volcanic activity in Indonesia, along with strengthened local safety and security measures, unpredictable circumstances have continued to develop. After discussions with the local promoter, we ultimately decided to cancel the concert with the safety of the artists and audience as our top priority. All tickets purchased will be fully refunded. Please refer to a separate announcement from the ticketing platform and local promoter for details regarding the refund process and schedule. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience and concern this cancellation may cause to the fans who have been looking forward to the concert, and we kindly ask for your understanding. Thank you. news.headline: Volcanic island in Indonesia erupts, canceling hundreds of flights and stranding thousands
news.body: Indonesia’s Anak Krakatau volcano has erupted, causing flight cancellations at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and stranding about 170,000 passengers in the region. The eruption happened early Sunday with volcanic ash affecting parts of western Indonesia. Indonesia’s Geological Agency reported that the volcano showed signs of activity since Friday, before the eruption. No casualties were reported, but authorities warned residents to stay at least 3 kilometers, or 2 miles, from the crater. Thousands of passengers were affected as airspace around several airports was closed. Indonesia’s Directorate General of Civil Aviation is closely monitoring the situation. The volcano remains active with officials evaluating the situation.
